title: Searching one large folder for a word that is in the folder's own name loses real matches
problem:
Found by the review of the whole branch (20 Nov), in which one reviewer read all the improvements together through one lens and a second reviewer tried to refute each finding against the code. Nothing was run in that review: every finding was traced by reading. [folder-search-pool-filled-by-folders-own-path] Searching one large folder for a word that is in the folder's own path loses real matches: fff-search fills the pool with matches the engine then discards. The finder's scenario: Steps: a search location /data; the folder /data/work holds more than about 4,000 items; turn on Search Only in "work" and type `work`. Same shape: `photo` in Photos, `doc` in Documents, `contoso` in `OneDrive - Contoso`.

What happens: the folder reaches fff-search as a glob constraint, which narrows the files but not the text matched. fff-search still matches the word against each item's path from the search location down, and that path begins with `work/`. Every item in the folder is therefore a match with one score: 60 for `work` (4 x 12, plus frizbee's prefix bonus of 12). A real `zz/workshop` scores 52 in its own name, and frizbee reports the first best alignment, so it gets no name bonus. fff returns 4,000 of them (files newest first, folders in path order). `through_ties` sees the tie run past those and keeps 2,000; in the window's Any Kind search files and folders take turns, so about half of each. The strict check then reads the path inside the folder, drops everything that matched only through `work/`, and lists what is left: the real matches that happened to be among the newest files or first folders. If none is, and Allow typos is on, the near-miss fallback finds nothing either: No Results, "The search looked only in work", and no `+`.

Files with the word in their own name are rescued by fff-search's filename pass only while the folder has at most 15,000 files. Folders, and files matched through an inner folder's name, never are.

What should happen: every item whose path inside the folder has the word is listed. The manual sentence added by 5624239 says "A search of only one folder looks in the path inside the folder searched, so the folder's own name doesn't count".

How new it is: plainly named folders behaved this way on upstream too. Folders with a space or one of `*?[]{}!\` in their path were fetched 20,000 wide until 5ebf1cf removed that, so for them (`My Documents`, `Google Drive`, `OneDrive - Contoso`) this is a regression between about 4,000 and 20,000 items. It is the recorded "cut before the strict check" limit, but here it holds for every item of the folder and for correctly spelled words.

Not run: the scores and thresholds are read from the fff-search and neo_frizbee sources. The code path: crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:1061-1069 (the folder goes to fff as Constraint::Glob only) -> :1092-1099 (`fetch` is (limit*4).max(2_000) unless wide or one letter; the folder over-fetch was dropped in 5ebf1cf) -> :1135-1137, :1157-1179, :1208-1210 (fff search, then `through_ties`) -> :2647-2661 (`through_ties` falls back to `fetch` when the tie runs past what fff returned) -> :2685-2712 (`best_of_both` takes a file and a folder in turn on equal scores) -> :1226-1234 (`rel` is the path inside the searched folder) -> :990-1002 (strict check and near-miss fallback read `rel`). fff-search-0.11.0/src/score.rs:54-90 (words matched on the whole relative path), :482-497 (a folder gets its name bonus only when the match starts in its last segment), :661 (filename pass off above 15,000 path matches), :734. neo_frizbee-0.13.3/src/const.rs:6-7 (prefix 12, delimiter 4); src/smith_waterman/algo/mod.rs:196 (`>` keeps the first best alignment). The second reviewer, who tried to refute it and confirmed it, corrects the scenario: As reported, with these limits. The threshold is the pool, fetch + 2,000: more than 4,000 matching items at Results shown 500 or less, 6,000 at 1,000, 10,000 at 2,000, and 22,000 at 5,000 or with a Nushell filter on. With Any Kind, folders and files take turns in the pool, so all of the folder's subfolders are kept while there are fewer than about 1,000 of them. On upstream, plainly named folders lost the same matches from 2,000 items; with Allow typos on, the list then showed the folder's newest items in their place, where the branch says No Results. For folders with a space or a glob character the loss is new only where the old 20,000 of the whole search location held the folder's items. Their evidence: Traced by reading; nothing was run. crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:1069 hands the folder to fff-search only as a filter: `let scope_filter = scope_glob.as_deref().map(Constraint::Glob);`. In fff-search-0.11.0/src/score.rs:608-618 the constraints only narrow `working_files`, and :649-655 match the words on each file's whole path from the search location down. So `work` scores 4 x 12 plus the prefix bonus of 12 = 60 for every item under `work/` (neo_frizbee-0.13.3/src/const.rs:1, 6, 7; smith_waterman/algo/ascii.rs:49-53 and 98-101), against 52 for a `workshop` further in. engine.rs:1092-1099: `(limit * 4).max(2_000)` and `let asked = fetch.saturating_add(TIES_AHEAD);`, so 4,000 are asked for. fff-search returns ties newest first (score.rs:1038-1042). engine.rs:2656-2657 `if end == scores.len() && matched > end { fetch }` keeps 2,000 when the tie runs past what was returned. engine.rs:1226-1233 makes `rel` the path inside the folder (`let searched = scope.as_deref().unwrap_or(&base);` then `strip_prefix(searched)`), and :990-1002 keep only hits with the words, or a near miss of them, in `rel`. No second fetch follows, so a real match outside the 2,000 kept is not listed, and the list is empty when none of the 2,000 passes. score.rs:661 (`path_matches.len() > 15_000`) is where the filename pass that rescues files by their own name stops. The only test of a word in the searched folder's own name has two files (engine.rs:4348). On record so far: the cut before the strict check, for typo matches that score like real ones (result-tie-break, Found, not fixed; final-pass-notes line 55). The folder's own path as the cause, for correctly spelled words and down to an empty list, is in no record, so I count it as worse than recorded and not as known.
proposal: Reproduce each fault first with a test that fails on the trunk. Then fix it. The finder's suggested fixes, as starting points and not checked plans: [folder-search-pool-filled-by-folders-own-path] In `search_root`, fetch wide (`limit.max(20_000)`, as for a one-letter or quoted search) when a folder inside the root is searched and every fuzzy word of two bytes or more has its letters in order in the folder's own path inside the location (the lowercased `scope.strip_prefix(&base)`). Those are exactly the searches whose pool fff fills with matches the check discards. That covers folders up to about 20,000 items. A complete fix would page on with `PaginationArgs.offset` while the strict check leaves fewer than `limit` hits and `total_matched` exceeds what was fetched.
original_test_plan: The finder's test ideas: [folder-search-pool-filled-by-folders-own-path] Engine test: a root with `work/f-0000.txt` to `work/f-4099.txt` and `work/old/workflows/ci.yml`, whose modification time is set a day back with `File::set_modified`. Search { query: "work", scope: root/work, files_only: true, limit: 10 } and expect ["ci.yml"]. By reading, today it returns nothing: the 4,000 newest tie, 2,000 are kept, and none has w-o-r-k inside the folder. A second case: 4,100 folders `work/d-NNNN` plus `work/zz/workshop`, Kind Folder, expecting ["workshop"]. Why the existing tests miss it: [folder-search-pool-filled-by-folders-own-path] Every test that searches a folder for a word in its own name uses a folder of two or three files (engine.rs:4348 `catalog` in Catalog, 4486-4553 `invoice` in invoices), where the whole folder is in the pool. The crowding tests (engine.rs:6114 name search, 6059 content search) put the better matches outside the folder, which the glob now keeps out. No test has more items inside the searched folder than the pool keeps while the word is in the folder's own path.
original_risks: This is a fix late in the branch: keep it to the fault. Every test on the trunk has to keep passing, and the improvements involved (result-tie-break, scoped-search-special-folder-names, strict-check-scope-relative, typo-fallback-near-miss) have tests that pin the behaviour around the fault: read their done records in /home/user/polish-tools/done/ before changing the functions they changed.

verifier.claim_check: A second reviewer traced the same path and confirmed it; neither ran anything. Reproduce before changing anything; if a test shows the fault is not there, write the closed record with the evidence and return skipped.

orchestrator_notes: This fault was in the app before this branch, at least in part: write a normal `Changelog (Fixed):` paragraph for what a user of the last release would notice. The full findings, with the second reviewer's evidence line by line, are in /home/user/polish-tools/review/*.md and *.json (search for the finding ids in brackets). The review read the branch at 7e8df53; other changes have landed since, so read the functions as they are now. Take the finder's first fix, the wide fetch for exactly these searches, and not the paging. 'scoped-search-special-folder-names' (5ebf1cf) removed a wide fetch for folders with special characters in their path and its done record says why; 'result-tie-break' (d85ca95) added `TIES_AHEAD` and `through_ties` and lists the fixtures sized against `fetch`; 'near-miss-beside-scattered' and 'accented-names-search' are landing in the same file just before you, so read `Engine::search` and `search_root` as they are after them. Measure what the wide fetch costs for such a search on a large tree and say so. For plainly named folders this was so before the branch: write a normal Changelog (Fixed) paragraph.
